name: ChartQA
description: A large-scale benchmark for question answering about charts with visual and logical reasoning. It covers 9,608 human-written questions (ChartQA-H) and 23,111 machine-generated questions (ChartQA-M) from human-written chart summaries, spanning 20,882 charts curated from four different online sources (Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data, OECD). The benchmark focuses on compositional and visual reasoning questions involving arithmetic and logical operations over real-world charts.
license: Publicly available charts used in compliance with respective source terms and conditions (Statista, Pew Research, OECD, OWID open access terms).
creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
publisher: York University, Canada; Nanyang Technological University, Singapore; Salesforce Research
citeAs: Masry, A., Long, D. X., Tan, J. Q., Joty, S., & Hoque, E. (2022). ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning. arXiv:2203.10244.
rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four different online sources: Statista (statista.com), Pew Research (pewresearch.org), Our World In Data or OWID (ourworldindata.org), and OECD (oecd.org). For Pew, only chart images were crawled since underlying data tables are not available. For the other three sources, underlying data tables, metadata (e.g., title, chart type), SVG files, and associated text descriptions were extracted. Bounding box information of chart elements was extracted from SVG files to train data extraction models. Human-authored QA pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT). Machine-generated QA pairs were generated from human-written Statista chart summaries using a fine-tuned T5 model.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For the Pew dataset, underlying data tables are not available, so only chart images were crawled. The T5 question generation model may generate invalid or incomplete questions due to domain mismatch; a heuristic filter was applied to remove questions whose answers cannot be found in the chart data table. After filtering, 86.64% of machine-generated QA pairs were found to be complete, answerable, and correct. The test set of the machine-generated dataset was manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Charts and associated data from four online sources: Statista (statista.com), Pew Research (pewresearch.org), Our World In Data (ourworldindata.org), and OECD (oecd.org). Human-written chart summaries from Statista were used for machine-generated QA pairs. Human-authored QA pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For machine-generated QA pairs, a pre-trained T5 model was fine-tuned on the SQuAD QA dataset and applied to human-written Statista chart summaries. Two T5 models were used: one for answer extraction (trained on SQuAD passage-answer pairs) and one for answer-aware question generation (trained on SQuAD passage-answer-question triples). A heuristic filter removed questions whose answers could not be found in the chart data table. The test set was manually cleaned to remove invalid questions. For VL-T5 visual features, Mask R-CNN with Resnet-101 was used to extract visual features of chart marks, padded to a fixed length of 36.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Chart images were parsed using an adapted ChartOCR model to extract underlying data tables. The CRAFT model was used to recognize texts in chart elements. Data values were associated with text labels using positional and color information. Bounding box information was extracted from SVG files. For machine-generated questions, a heuristic filter removed questions whose answers could not be found in the chart data table. The dataset was randomly split into train, validation, and test sets for both ChartQA-H and ChartQA-M. Visual features for VL-T5 were extracted using Mask R-CNN fine-tuned on chart element detection (15 object classes), initialized with pre-trained COCO weights.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human-authored QA annotation was conducted via Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT). In each HIT, workers verified two previously asked questions by other workers and provided two new QA pairs per chart image. Workers were asked to focus on two types of questions: compositional questions (requiring at least two mathematical/logical operations such as sum, difference, average) and visual questions (referring to visual attributes such as color, height, length of graphical marks). For each chart, workers provided two questions with answers. The same questions were then answered by another annotator. If both workers' answers exactly matched, the answer was considered correct; otherwise, answers were manually checked to select the final correct answer. Workers were selected with an acceptance rate of 95% and at least 5,000 accomplished HITs, and further filtered via a pretest. Machine-generated QA pairs were generated from human-written Statista summaries using a fine-tuned T5 model, and a subset was manually validated for quality assurance.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between crowd workers based on exact matches was 61.04%. Manual checking of 500 random samples found agreement to be 78.55% when considering typos and lexical variations (e.g., '3$' vs '3 dollars', '86.33' vs '86.3'). For machine-generated questions, 1,250 QA pairs were manually analyzed and 86.64% were found to be complete, answerable, and correct given the chart. For the extended VisionTaPas difference/ratio operation supervision, manual checking of 100 such questions showed 24% noise with the heuristics used.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 questions per chart (each answered by two annotators); for machine-generated, questions were generated automatically and a subset manually validated.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with an acceptance rate of 95% and at least 5,000 accomplished HITs, further filtered via a pretest. Workers were compensated at or above the U.S. minimum wage ($7.25 USD per hour), receiving $0.6 USD per task (estimated 3-5 minutes per task). All annotations were anonymized to protect annotator privacy.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: T5 model (fine-tuned on SQuAD) for answer extraction and question generation from human-written chart summaries; ChartOCR (Luo et al., 2021) for automatic chart data extraction; CRAFT model (Baek et al., 2019) for text recognition in chart elements; Mask R-CNN with Resnet-101 for visual feature extraction; detectron2 library for object detection.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/vis-nlp/ChartQA. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described in the paper.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive human attributes are collected as part of this dataset. Annotator annotations were anonymized to protect annotator privacy.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to advance Chart Question Answering systems that help users analyze data visualizations. The authors note that models can be abused to mislead the public about chart content and implications, and that model outputs cannot be guaranteed to be correct at all times.
rai:dataBiases: Politics is a common topic among all sources, particularly in the Pew dataset where nearly half of charts are about U.S. Politics & Policy (45.4%). Bar charts are the most common chart type across all datasets. The dataset is constructed from four specific online sources, which may introduce topic and style biases. Machine-generated questions are derived solely from Statista human-written summaries.
rai:dataLimitations: Most answers to machine-generated questions are values/labels of chart elements, limiting answer diversity. The T5 question generation model may generate invalid or incomplete questions due to domain mismatch. Data extraction accuracy is lower for real-world charts with diverse styles, especially pie charts and charts with logarithmic scales or very large values. Evaluation metrics for chart data extraction do not take extracted textual tokens into consideration. Models cannot effectively handle nested arithmetic operations. The benchmark covers only bar, line, and pie chart types.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing of Chart Question Answering (ChartQA) models. The benchmark is designed to evaluate visual and logical reasoning over real-world charts, including compositional and visual question types. It can also be used for pretraining and fine-tuning transformer-based QA models. The dataset is intended for academic research purposes.
